correctness.rationale: The variational spectral quotient is min_z (∑w_i z_i²)/(z^T[diag(p)-pp^T]z), with V positive definite by pi_0>0. Substitution x_i=w_i/gap gives the primal SDP min∑c_i x_i s.t. diag(x)-V PSD; strict primal feasibility and Gram dual diag(Y)=c yield dual S-min||∑pi_i u_i||². The sharp polygon resultant lower bound is delta, attained by planar closing or collinear opposite vectors. For delta=0, x=p, slack ppT rank1, complementary slackness with nonzero Gram vectors forces uniqueness. For delta>0, explicit x_j=pi_j(1-delta/sqrt(c_j)) and x_i=pi_i(1+delta/sqrt(c_i)) produce a PSD slack by positive leaf-away-from-j Schur block with zero complement, rank m-1; rank-one dual kernel forces uniqueness. Budget-normalize by T and get required multiplicities. All positivity and transition boundary cases were checked.

value.rationale: A complete and sharp optimization classification on the canonical star graph under two physically meaningful heterogeneities (vertex occupancy masses and per-edge conductance costs) determines all optimal rates, sharp phase boundary, uniqueness and eigengap multiplicity; mass imbalance causes a transition even with equal prices. Not merely a fixed example, parameter renaming or known unweighted-star evaluation.

final_claim: For a finite reversible continuous-time star with m≥3 leaves, strictly positive stationary masses pi, independent positive edge prices c and budget ∑c_i w_i=1, the optimal L2(pi) gap is 1/(S-delta²), S=∑pi_i c_i and delta=(2 max_i(pi_i sqrt(c_i))-∑pi_i sqrt(c_i))_+, with unique explicit conductances and multiplicity m-1 (polygon) versus 1 (imbalance).
limitations: Not discrete-time SLEM, capped rates or zero-mass models.
